Decision.Title: ## D23 — pilot is decided on `supersedeChainDepth`, not on the amendment count
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-02 by the maintainer**, on [F139](#f139), at the close of `C-AMENDMENT-COUNT` — the moment [D22.1](#d22.1) names as the end of the deliberate collection, when pilot becomes decidable.
**The premise that forced the decision.** `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL:80` calls the amendment count "the measuring instrument". The instrument now exists and works — a synthetic re-ratification reads 1, a revert reads 2 — and it reads **zero on every bundle in the corpus**. That zero is honest: verified independently of the derivation by parsing all 53 ledgers on disk, no bundle has ever had an approved spec or plan amended and re-approved at a changed fingerprint. This project does not correct by amending; when a spec is wrong it supersedes the whole bundle. The correction cost is carried entirely by `supersedeChainDepth`, which reads > 0 on 8 of 59 change objects.
**The variants put to the maintainer, and why the runners-up lose.**
| | Variant | For | Against | |---|---|---|---| | **A** | **Decide pilot on `supersedeChainDepth`**; treat the amendment counter as instrumentation for a mechanism not yet used. | Uses the signal the project actually generates. Costs nothing and delays nothing. Keeps both counters meaning exactly one thing. | The pilot's own wording named amendments, so the criterion is being read against a different number than it says. | | **B** | Widen the instrument to report both costs under one heading. | Makes the number legible at a glance without knowing which verb the project uses. | [D21](#d21) forbids conflating two costs in a derivation that must represent the operation truthfully. Buys presentation with a schema ruling. | | **C** | Defer pilot until `C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY-2` produces the first non-zero `reRatificationCount`. | Truest to the criterion as written; decides on the named number rather than a substitute. | That bundle is last in the order, so it pays a full branch of delay for a single data point — and one datum would not make the count informative anyway. |
**Ruled: A.** The counter stays as built and stays honest. **Its zero must never be read as "amendment is cheap"** — it means amendment is not the correction verb here, and a future reader who forgets that will draw the opposite conclusion from the same number.
**What this does not do.** It does not change the derivation, retitle either counter, or amend `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL`. `reRatificationCount` remains bundle-internal and `supersedeChainDepth` cross-bundle, exactly as `C-AMENDMENT-COUNT` shipped them. If this project ever starts amending approved artifacts in place, the instrument is already there and the reading flips back without code.
**Sequencing note.** The ruling was given while the executor held the tree for the `C-REASON-CONSTANTS` plan and was recorded once that plan landed, so the write could not surface in that bundle's scope audit as a new out-of-scope file.

Decision.Title: ## D25 — a CI-red hotfix on an unmerged branch does not require a change bundle
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-02 by the maintainer**, on the [F146](#f146) fix committed at `4004170`, when `.ngrace/changes/active` was empty and no bundle owned the write.
**The ruling, as given: hotfix.** The write stands ungoverned, and this entry is the record that explains why a production edit exists with no spec, no plan, and no ledger.
**Why a retro-bundle was the wrong alternative.** The choice was between leaving the write governed by nothing and authoring a bundle after the fact to describe a change that had already happened. The second is worse: a spec written to match a completed diff cannot fail, its `BaselineAssertions` describe a tree that no longer exists, and its ledger would record an execution that never occurred. That is a **fabricated** governance record, and this repository's whole product is the claim that its records are not fabricated. Ungoverned-and-labelled beats governed-and-false.
**The boundary — this is the authority's derivation from a one-word ruling, not the maintainer's own words, and he should correct it if it reaches too far.** The exemption covers a change that is *all* of the following:
- **on an unmerged branch**, never on `main`; - **restoring a red CI to green**, not adding capability; - **test-or-tooling only**, with no production behaviour change — `4004170` touched one `.test.ts` file and nothing that ships; - **verified in both directions**, so the repaired test is shown to still discriminate rather than merely to pass.
It does **not** license ungoverned production edits, convenience fixes bundled alongside a hotfix, or skipping a bundle because one looks expensive. `C-GOVERNANCE-ORDER` — refuse a write with no approved change that owns it — remains named and unscheduled in the registry; when it ships, this exemption is the case it must be taught to allow, and this entry is the specification of that carve-out.
**Precedent shape.** [D11](#d11) refuses deferral without a dependency or a conflict, and [F145](#f145) records that a defect found is a defect fixed before the work is handed on. A red CI on an unmerged branch is a conflict in D11's sense: the branch cannot proceed, and the governed path has no active bundle to attach the repair to. The exemption resolves that deadlock rather than widening the path.

Decision.Title: ## D26 — an unfalsifiable criterion is reworded, and evidence-discrimination becomes its own bundle
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-02 by the maintainer**, on [F147](#f147), in two parts.
**Part 1 — `AC-PROTOCOL-COMMIT-BODY` is reworded, variant C of three.** The criterion bound a commit-message claim to `git log --format=%B`, which exits 0 unconditionally, so the gate would have archived a pass it never tested. Rejected: **A**, replacing the command with a filtering assertion script — it pays a script and a wider write surface for something no other bundle has needed; **B**, dropping the criterion outright — it discards a real intent.
Under C the criterion becomes **`AC-CHANGELOG-UNTOUCHED`**, keeping the verifiable half (D5.5: `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited) with `git diff --exit-code e5aced5 -- CHANGELOG.md`, **probed in both directions before the rewrite**: 0 unedited, 1 on a staged edit, 0 restored. The commit-body expectation moves to the execution brief as an instruction. **A requirement that cannot be refuted at close does not become a criterion just because it is important** — it becomes a brief.
**Part 2 — the lint gap gets its own bundle, `C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION`.** Not grafted into `C-REWORK-CIRCUIT`, which already forces four modules. Name searched before minting: the territory holds `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE` (which created the `CloseEvidence` state), `C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE`, `C-COMMAND-EVIDENCE-RECORDED`, `C-FOLD-USES-RECORDED-COMMAND-EVIDENCE` and `C-VERDICT-EVIDENCE`; **none covers whether a recorded command can fail.**
**Design constraints that bundle inherits, and the maintainer's correction that produced them.** The authority first objected that the proposed allowlist named `vitest`, `jest` and `eslint`, none of which this repository uses. **That objection was parochial and was withdrawn**: neo-grace is the marketplace package, and the rule ships to consumer projects whose toolchains are their own — what is installed *here* says nothing about what the rule must accept *there*. `CLAUDE.md`'s first line says exactly this, and the authority grepped the local `package.json` as though this were an application.
What survives, and is strengthened by that reframe:
- **Allowlist by command *shape*, never a denylist of binaries.** Measured: `git diff` exits 0 on a dirty tree, `git diff --exit-code` exits 1. **The flag decides, not the binary**, so banning `git` would reject the discriminating form already used by `C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY-2`'s `T-006`, and banning `git log` would still miss `git show`, `head`, `printf`, `find` and `true`. A denylist fails open; across arbitrary consumer projects the non-assertive space is unbounded. - **Config-driven and polyglot by default.** `.ngrace-lint.json` already carries `codeExtensions`, `unverifiedLanguages`, `gateFailOn` and `ignoredDirs`, and six language adapters ship. A hardcoded set would be wrong for most consumers. - **Warning severity with a documented escape.** `AC-CLOSE-LINT` runs `--fail-on warnings`, so a warning still blocks any close that has not justified itself, without making a novel discriminating command unauthorable. - **Command text only.** `C-PHASE-RULE-PIN`'s charter and [decisions.md:7525](#) both hold that the restriction must not resolve package scripts transitively — the explicitly rejected reading B. The rule may not open a consumer's `package.json`, `Makefile` or `justfile`, so *"a script designed to exit non-zero"* is an intent claim the linter cannot check; only shape is checkable.
**The limit, and it must be written into the rule's own `--explain` text.** Well-known runners have non-assertive modes — `pytest --collect-only`, `cargo test --no-run`, `go test -run` matching nothing all exit 0 — so an allowlist catches only the cheap class. `git diff --exit-code` over the *wrong paths* passes any linter and proves nothing. **The linter catches the cheap class; the authority runs the command against a violating tree before approving.** A green rule must not be read as evidence that the harder check happened.

Decision.Title: ### D26.1 correction — five language adapters ship, not six. **[verified]**
Decision.Body:
[D26](#d26) states *"six language adapters ship"* as a premise for the polyglot-defaults constraint. **That is false at HEAD.** Reported by the executor while authoring `C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION`'s spec and re-measured independently by the authority on **2026-09-03** at `42aa4df`:
``` bun -e 'import {LANGUAGE_ADAPTERS} from "./src/language-registry.ts"; console.log(LANGUAGE_ADAPTERS.length)' → 5 # js-ts, python, dart, go, rust ```
`README.md`'s language table lists the same five. **`dart`, `go` and `rust` carry no test-runner constant**, so a default shape table cannot derive `dart test`, `go test` or `cargo test` from an adapter export; those three come from D26's own prose instead, and the spec records that derivation rather than inventing adapter exports.
**D26's ruling is unaffected and stands in full.** The count was decorative — the constraint is that defaults must be polyglot and config-driven *because the rule ships to consumer toolchains*, and that reasoning does not depend on whether five or six adapters ship. **This is a correction to a premise, not an overturning of a decision.**
Recorded because the evidence standard requires it: when the executor corrects a number, the authority re-measures independently and **records the correction against the artifact that carried it**. Also noted: [F147](#f147)'s *"All 19 `CloseEvidence` commands in the corpus"* was true when written and is now stale — **25 Command children / 11 distinct across 61 specs** at this HEAD (23 / 9 across 60, excluding `C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION`'s own draft). [F123](#f123): a corpus count expires the moment a bundle archives, so it is re-measured at citation, never quoted from an earlier turn.

Decision.Title: ## D27 — an approved governance artifact is repaired by supersede, not by amend-and-re-ratify, until pilot is decided
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-04 by the maintainer**, on [F157](#f157)'s remedy: *"supercede. record decision so d25 will not confuse in the future. let's wait until we reach pilot phase. we might consider hot fix relaxed or something else."*
**The ruling.** When an approved spec or plan is found defective, the route is **`ngrace supersede`** and a replacement bundle. **Amend-and-re-ratify is not available.** The CLI permits it — measured in both directions, [F157](#f157) — and `C-AMENDMENT-COUNT` counts it, but permitted is not authorised: the bounded-amendment regime is [`RM-PILOT-APPROVAL`](../RM-PILOT-APPROVAL/review.md), whose plan is **`_not written_`** and which is **"Not scheduled, deliberately"** pending two to three more bundles of data. Until it is decided, an amendment to an approved artifact is an unratified governance mode.
**What was done before this ruling, recorded rather than tidied away.** On 2026-09-04 the authority amended `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION`'s approved plan and had it re-ratified, producing this repository's **first non-zero `reRatificationCount`** — exactly `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL`'s first constraint (*"every amendment re-ratifies with its own phrase and fingerprint"*) executed without pilot existing. The commits stand; they are a true record of a misstep and are **not** rewritten. This entry is what explains them.
**D25 does not reach this case, and that is the confusion this entry exists to prevent.** [D25](#d25) exempts a **CI-red hotfix on an unmerged branch** where *"the governed path has no active bundle to attach the repair to"* — it was decided when `.ngrace/changes/active` was **empty**. That condition is load-bearing, not incidental. A bundle whose own approved plan is defective **has** an owner — itself — and the governed remedy exists, so no exemption is needed and none is granted. D25 covers a red CI with **no eligible bundle**; it does not cover repairing governance, and it never licenses editing an artifact's approved bytes.
**Why the stale test pin is not patched under an exemption either.** `src/grace-status.test.ts:1153` asserts `reRatificationCount` is 0 for every change in the live repository, which the re-ratification falsified. It is a **dated corpus measurement** — `C-AMENDMENT-COUNT`'s plan words it as *"Live-repo: `collectProjectStatus` on this repository reports `reRatificationCount 0` on every change"*, in the same idiom as the `expectedDepth` table beside it — not a governance tripwire. The **replacement bundle carries the correction in its own `ObservedWriteScope`**, fully governed. The circularity that blocked this inside the defective bundle does not exist for a fresh one: a first approve per artifact is baseline 0 ([`AC-SPEC-PLUS-PLAN`](../../../../.ngrace/changes/archive/C-AMENDMENT-COUNT/spec.xml)), the fix is test-only, and `*.test.ts` is not module-ownable (`isModuleOwnableWritePath`), so pulling in a test file from another area forces no module into `AffectedAreas` and raises no [F136](#f136) shape.
**The cost, recorded as the pilot datum it is.** One wrong sentence in an approved plan, found by executing it, costs: a replacement bundle authored and approved at two stages, a supersede, a revert of correct production so the replacement's reds can genuinely fail, and a re-execution. That is precisely the arithmetic `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL` was written to argue about, and this instance is of its **motivating class** — *"a defect only running the code can reveal"*. **It is one datum and it is confounded**: it came from an authority error, not from a review miss, the same confound [F134](#f134) records for the pre-approval amendments. It does not decide pilot, and [D23](#d23) holds — pilot is decided on `supersedeChainDepth`.
**Left open, explicitly.** A relaxed-hotfix or bounded-amendment carve-out may be considered **when pilot is reached**, not before. Nothing in this entry authorises one.

Decision.Title: ## D28 — `decisions.md` is retired into three genres, each with a retirement rule and a size ratchet
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-05 by the maintainer**, on the rationale question he put to the authority: *"we need to retire decisions.md. Your 3 parts suggestion looks good. One important thing is to make sure that they will not grow forever. We need to provide ability to make those parts manageable. Some kind of retire/decay routine."*
**The ruling.** The single append-only document is replaced by **three genres** — findings, decisions, registry — and **each carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet**. Growth without retirement is the defect being fixed; a split alone would reproduce it three times.
**Not a structure question, a lifecycle question.** The parts are the enabling change. The deliverable is that every entry has an **observable retirement trigger** and every live part has a **budget that refuses to grow**. Chartered as [`C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`](#named-bundle-registry), **position 2** of the order ratified 2026-09-04, which shifts `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` to 3, `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` to 4, `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` to 5 and `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` to 6.
**Enforcement ships with the structure, never after it.** If sizing forces a split, the validator lands first or alongside — an unenforced convention is exactly how this file reached 9940 lines.

Decision.Title: ### D28.1 — the enforcement shape, and the decisions genre retires on codification. **[ratified]**
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-05 by the maintainer**, in two parts, on itemized variants put to him.
**Findings and the registry take the paired shape: eligibility is the enforcement, the ceiling is the backstop.** An entry that is **eligible for retirement and still live** is an **error**, reported per entry and naming the event that made it eligible; that rule carries no number, so no number can be raised to pass it. Each live part *also* carries a **ceiling** with headroom, whose failure message names the retirement operation rather than the config key. In normal operation the eligibility rule keeps every part far below its ceiling, so the ceiling fires only when retirement is being dodged — which is exactly when it is wanted. **The rejected shape was a line budget as the sole enforcement**: it bites at an arbitrary moment during legitimate work, names no specific entry as the remedy, and the cheapest way out of it is a config edit. Ceiling rather than cliff is [D24](#d24)'s vocabulary, taken deliberately.
**The decisions genre retires on codification, not on being overturned.** The maintainer's ruling, recorded verbatim: *"A decision moves from live to retired when its prose invariant is permanently replaced by an automated machine check. Trigger: The decision is tagged with `codifiedIn: <lint-rule | test-suite>` (e.g., when D24 is codified into the C-REWORK-CIRCUIT gate). Rationale: The text is no longer needed in the live reading set because the compiler/linter now enforces the boundary unconditionally."*
This replaces the *"a later decision overturns it and names it"* trigger proposed in [F161](#f161)'s table, which was rare enough to leave the genre growing monotonically. Overturning remains **a** way a decision leaves the live set; it is no longer the only one.
**Two resolution checks make the tag evidence rather than a claim, and they ship with it, not after.**
1. **The pointer must resolve.** A `codifiedIn` naming a lint rule id absent from the catalog, or a test that does not exist, is an **error**. Without it a decision retires by *asserting* a check — [F147](#f147)'s manufactured-pass shape moved from close evidence onto governance. 2. **Removing the named check must fail.** Deleting or renaming a rule or test that a live `codifiedIn` tag names is an **error** while the tag stands. This is what makes *"permanently"* mechanical rather than aspirational: a retired invariant whose enforcement was quietly dropped is unenforced **and** unread, which is worse than either alone.
**Consequence for the spec.** This is the only one of the three triggers that requires evidence of a **machine** rather than an event, which makes it the strongest of the three rather than the weakest — but only with both checks above. The population it acts on is **measured, never assumed**: how many live decisions state an invariant that is already codified today is an open count, and the maintainer's own example — [D24](#d24) against `C-REWORK-CIRCUIT`'s ceiling — is a **candidate to verify**, not a fact to restate ([F123](#f123)).

Decision.Title: ## D29 — this repository adopts function contracts on its governed surface, and the module baseline becomes a gate first
Decision.Body:
**Ruled 2026-09-05 by the maintainer** on four itemized variants ([F162](#f162)), selecting adoption of a load-bearing subset with enforcement, over full adoption, exemption-and-record, and a second deferral.
**In scope for `START_CONTRACT:`** — the command surface and public engine facade (any declaration exported from a top-level command handler), and **state-machine and ledger boundaries**: any function that writes, transitions, or validates audit state, ledger records, or git operations — the core governance pipeline.
**Excluded** — internal leaf helpers, utility transformers, and purely local file-scoped helpers.
**Block markers are reserved for complex control flow** — multi-step validations, rollback ladders, transaction scopes. **Disallowed in flat sequential logic**, where they only duplicate the visual shape of the function body.
**The baseline becomes a gate before any function contract is written.** The maintainer's reasoning, recorded: *"The fact that the linter validates `LINKS:` only if a contract exists is the classic conditional validator defect… If someone adds `src/review/new-gate.ts` tomorrow with zero markup, the repo stays green while silently dropping out of governance."*
- **Rule:** `require-module-contract`. **Predicate:** every file matching `src/**/*.ts`, excluding `.test.ts`, fixtures, and explicitly ignored shims, must begin with a valid `START_MODULE_CONTRACT` header. **Cost:** near zero — the tree is already 65/65, so turning it on needs no remediation diff today and locks the baseline permanently. - The catalog namespaces rule ids by family (`markup.*`, `graph.*`, `change.*`); the spec picks a conforming id rather than the bare name used here.
**Phasing and order.** The gate is a narrow, leaf-level verification fix with **zero file remediation**, so it takes **position 3**, behind `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`, patching the structural blind spot immediately and preventing regression while the larger retirement work proceeds. Function-contract adoption is a **downstream bundle** whose validator rule ships **simultaneously with its initial target annotations** — never annotations first and enforcement later ([D28](#d28)'s rule, applied to the product).
**Renumbering.** Inserting the gate at 3 and the rollout at the tail shifts the ratified order to: **1** `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION` (delivered) → **2** `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` → **3** `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` → **4** `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` → **5** `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` → **6** `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` → **7** `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` → **8** `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE`. Relative order is otherwise untouched.
**Not decided here**, and left open rather than assumed: the 35 unmarked `src/*.test.ts` files, and whether this repository claims `rust.md:60-62`'s trace-assertion permission in place of the logging convention. Both want a ruling; neither is in the two bundles above.

Decision.Title: ## D30 — the record freezes for the lifetime of a bundle that measures it, and ceilings become formulas
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-05 by the maintainer** on [F163](#f163), as the only coherent stance of three offered.
**Freeze, as discipline.** `decisions.md` is frozen for the lifecycle of `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`. [F161.1](#f161.1), [F163](#f163), this decision, and any finding raised while the bundle is open are held in an untracked buffer at `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` and flush to the live record at close or immediately post-archive. The buffer path is `.gitignore`d so a `git add -A` cannot sweep it into a public repository.
**Dynamic derivation, as schema invariant.** A spec may not pin scalar counts of a file it changes into its hard `Constraints`. Ceilings are stated as formulas over a baseline measured **at execution time** — `ceiling = base + headroom` — and computed by the tool during the retirement pass, never transcribed. Dated measurements remain legitimate as *context*; what is forbidden is a `Constraint` whose truth expires the next time anyone writes the file.
**The freeze lifts on the schema fix, not on the archive** — ratified 2026-09-05 when the maintainer agreed the early lift is right. It has an observable trigger and two phases, because it was doing two jobs and the schema fix retires only one of them.
- **Job 1, stale constants** — a `Constraint` pinning a count that a later append falsifies. This is what [F163](#f163) actually recorded, and **dynamic derivation retires it entirely.** The trigger is observable: the freeze's first phase ends when the approved `spec.xml` contains no pinned scalar count of `decisions.md` in its hard `Constraints`, which a reader can check against the frozen artifact. - **Job 2, concurrent mutation** — the retirement pass is a **read-modify-write over the whole file**: it reads every heading and body, writes the genre files, and rewrites the index. An append landing inside that window is not merely stale, it can be **lost or duplicated**, and no schema change prevents it. So a narrow freeze re-tightens for the execution window in which the split runs, and for any dispatch the authority has already promised a frozen base to.
**The operative rule.** After the schema fix the authority may append **between dispatches**; it may never append **while a dispatch that reads or rewrites the record files is in flight**, and never after promising a frozen base in a brief that has already been handed over. Findings raised inside a window stay in this buffer until it closes.
**Right now the freeze holds in full**: the send-back brief for the spec revision was handed over promising `decisions.md` frozen at `b0adb69`, and that promise outranks the early lift.

Decision.Title: ## D31 — the record retirement is two bundles, and identity ships before the engine
Decision.Body:
**Decided 2026-09-05 by the maintainer**, who proposed the two-bundle cut on [D26](#d26)'s precedent against overloading a complex bundle, and accepted the authority's objection that the proposed **order** was inverted.
**The cut.** Identity first, engine second.
- **`C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`** — inject explicit `<a id>` anchors and resolve the ambiguous citations **while `decisions.md` is still one document**. Nothing moves. Carries the dot-preserving slug grammar (`F9.1 → f9.1`) as a stated rule, not as shipped code. - **`C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`** — the three-layer split (index / live / retired), the retirement operation with **dynamic ceiling derivation** ([D30](#d30)), and the `codifiedIn` **and `taughtIn`** forward and reverse resolution checks.
**Why the order was inverted, measured 2026-09-05 at `a6fefc0`, corrected by [F164](#f164).** **431 of 568** internal `(#f…)`/`(#d…)` occurrences sit **inside F/D bodies** — the text the split moves — and 137 sit elsewhere (15 preamble, 22 slip register, 100 registry). The authority first reported 408/160 from a region rule that misclassified non-F/D subsection headings inside a body as leaving it. The split is therefore the very act that converts 408 same-file anchors into cross-file references. Shipping the engine first leaves those 408 in an undefined state for the whole interval between the two bundles, which is exactly the window in which `(#f93)` resolves to the wrong finding ([F161.1](#f161.1)'s seventh fact). With identity settled first, the engine's rewrite is mechanical over a set whose every member has one unambiguous target, and a preservation criterion can assert that every anchor resolves both before and after.
**A deliverable with an empty population, removed from the cut.** The proposal asked the anchor bundle to *"verify inbound fragment resolution across all archived and live artifacts"*. Measured: **zero** archived artifacts cite a fragment — `grep -rhoE 'decisions\.md#[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' .ngrace/changes/archive/ docs/plans/` returns nothing, and all 22 literal-path and 45 filename citations are path-only. The real inbound surface is the 568 internal fragments. The criterion binds those.
**`taughtIn`, added here.** [D28.1](#d28.1)'s `codifiedIn` trigger reaches only decisions a machine can enforce. Classified at `a6fefc0`, roughly six of the 22 live H2 decisions qualify — D1, D3, D5, D7, D9 and D24 (implemented at `src/grace-cursor.ts:196`). The other sixteen are practice rules binding people and agents — D19, D20, D22, D23, D25, D26, D27, D28, D29 among them — which no lint rule can hold, leaving the ceiling as sole enforcement for three quarters of the genre, the shape D28.1 rejected. `taughtIn: <skill path + section>` is the parallel trigger: for a practice rule the machine is the skill text that carries it, already pinned by `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts`. **The same two resolution checks apply unchanged** — the pointer must resolve, and removing the pinned text must fail.
**Registry rows** (stage into the Named-bundle registry at flush): `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` at **position 2**, `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` moving to **position 3**, and every later position shifting by one — `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` 4, `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` 5, `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` 6, `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` 7, `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` 8, `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE` 9.

Decision.Title: ### D27.1 — supersede repairs a **ratified** artifact; an unratified draft is corrected in place. **[ratified]**
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-06 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"i agree with B and C later"*, on itemized variants put to him after [F176](#f176) showed the draft half was being cited as though [D27](#d27) said it.
**The ruling.** [D27](#d27)'s route — `ngrace supersede` plus a replacement bundle — governs an artifact the **run ledger records as approved**. An artifact that has never been approved is **corrected in place**: there is no ratification to invalidate and nothing to supersede. This is a statement of `D27`'s boundary, not a new permission; `D27` is silent on drafts, and the silence was being read as a sentence.
**The boundary is the ledger Decision and the fingerprint, never the `status` attribute.** The close ceremony hand-writes `status="applied"`, so the attribute is hand-editable; approval is not. Measured 2026-09-06 at `4bb299d`, both directions:
| probe | result | |---|---| | hand-write `status="approved"`, no `gate approve`, on a throwaway project | `review.approval-never-asked`, exit **1** — *"approved spec.xml has no applying permitting approve Decision"* | | perturb one byte of a properly approved `spec.xml` | `review.approved-fingerprint-mismatch`, exit **1** | | restore those bytes byte-identically | exit **0** | | edit a `draft` spec by any amount | no finding, exit **0** | | `ngrace status` on the hand-marked file | prints `spec=approved` and raises nothing — status **displays** the attribute, `review` **adjudicates** it |
`ngrace supersede` is also bundle-level by construction: it requires `--change` plus `--replacement` naming a *different already-existing* `C-*`, and it moves the whole bundle into `archive/`. It cannot express an artifact-level fix to an unratified draft without abandoning the bundle and minting a replacement for something nobody ratified.
**Born codified, and not intended to accumulate as live prose.** Both halves of the invariant are already enforced by shipped checks (`review.approval-never-asked`, `review.approved-fingerprint-mismatch`), so under [D28.1](#d28.1) this entry is a `codifiedIn` candidate the moment `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` ships the tag. That bundle populates **zero** historical tags by its own NonGoal, so the tagging belongs to the follow-on codify bundle, not to it.
**The teaching half is chartered, and no new name is minted.** The shipped skills scope the immutability rule to approved artifacts correctly and in every place — by explicit word in `ngrace-execute/SKILL.md:8` (*"Run `ngrace supersede` instead of editing an **approved** conflict in place"*) and `ngrace-explainer/references/contract-driven-dev.md:58`, and by enclosing element in `ngrace-plan/SKILL.md:29-31`, where *"do not refresh ... in place"* sits inside `<approved_plan_immutability>` beneath *"if `plan.xml` already exists with status `approved`"*. The defect is not a mis-scoped rule; it is that **the draft complement is stated nowhere**, so a reader who needs the permitted route finds only the forbidden one and reaches for `D27`. That complement belongs to [`C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY`](#named-bundle-registry) at **position 7** ([D34](#d34); 6 under [D32](#d32), 5 before that), whose charter row already names `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror and already quotes *"status remains draft"* and *"do not author `plan.xml` until approved"*. Searched before proposing a new name: `C-TEACHING-SURFACE`, `C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW`, `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE`, `C-CO-DRAFT`, `C-SUPERSEDE-VERB` and `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND` are archived or cover other ground; `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` is the existing home. **[D31](#d31)'s ratified order is unchanged** — nothing is inserted and no position shifts. Once that skill text lands, this entry also gains a `taughtIn` trigger under `D31`.

Decision.Title: ## D32 — `C-ROADMAP-XML` enters at position 4, and every later position shifts by one
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-06 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"4 it is"*, on itemized variants — insert at **4** against append at **10**.
**The order, in full after this amendment.** **1** `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION` (delivered as `-2`) → **2** `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` (delivered as `-2`, PR #72) → **3** `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` (live as `-2`) → **4** **`C-ROADMAP-XML`** (new) → **5** `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` → **6** `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` → **7** `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` → **8** `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` → **9** `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` → **10** `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE`. The insertion shifts six positions by one and **reorders nothing**; relative order is otherwise untouched, as in [D28](#d28), [D29](#d29) and [D31](#d31).
**Why 4 rather than the tail, measured 2026-09-06 at `408f2ae`.** **40 of 68** archived bundles cite a `docs/plans/active/<RM>/` path (rule: `grep -rl` over archived `spec.xml` and `plan.xml`, counted by bundle directory). Exposure to silent citation decay therefore accrues with nearly every bundle that archives, and [F177](#f177) is what that decay already looks like — 15 archived bundles citing a `plan.md` path that does not exist, undetected. The runner-up, appending at **10**, renumbers nothing and loses on exactly that: six bundles' worth of new citations written before any check exists. The cost of waiting is not the conversion, it is the citations written while waiting.
**What this amendment falsifies, swept with it rather than after it.** [D27.1](#d27.1) named `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` at **position 5**; it is **6** from here. Any text that names a position must be re-derived from this entry. An amendment that changes a numbering and does not name what it falsifies leaves known-false text standing elsewhere, which is the failure this paragraph exists to prevent.

Decision.Title: ## D33 — the close-order clause is taught in `ngrace-execute`, and `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE` carries it
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-06 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"B please"*, on three itemized variants — document it in the authority's own artifacts only; teach it in the skill; or change the product so a `command-run` cannot reset a terminal state.
**The ruling.** The clause is added to `skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` and its byte-identical packaged mirror, pinned by a `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts` assertion, under the **existing** chartered name [`C-APPROVAL-SCOPE`](#named-bundle-registry). **Searched before minting**, 2026-09-06 at `401db34`, over `registry.xml` and `registry-retired.xml`: that row already owns *"skill text for the per-step rule **and the authority-owned close"*, named by [D19](#d19) and [D20](#d20). **No new name is minted and [D32](#d32)'s order does not shift.**
**Why not the product change.** `command-run` → `in-progress` is a shipped, deliberate mapping under `C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE`, and correct for its ordinary use. Overturning it to prevent an operator ordering error would answer a one-clause teaching gap with a semantic change; [CLAUDE.md](../../../../CLAUDE.md) rule 9 requires answering the original argument, and nothing in [F179](#f179) does. If the fault recurs **after** the teaching ships, that recurrence is the evidence the product change would need.
**Why not documentation alone.** [F179](#f179) measured the fault twice — `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` and `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` — under a sequence that lives only in the authority's session prompt. Every other GRACE consumer runs the shipped skill, which is silent on the ordering, so a fix confined to this repository's private artifacts leaves the trap in the product.
**Scope discipline.** `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE`'s charter is broader than this clause: [D19](#d19) requires the skills to say that **an approval covers the current step only**, and [D20](#d20) that **the authority owns the close** — `--assertions final`, `review`, `gate verdict`, `gate apply`, `gate archive`, the `applied` writes, and the archive move. The close-order clause belongs inside D20's half. Whether the bundle discharges its **whole** charter or only this clause is a scoping decision for its spec, and the brief must put that question rather than assume it.
**Position.** The row is chartered and marked *"Ordered, not deferred"* yet appears in **no** position of [D31](#d31) or [D32](#d32)'s enumerated order — an inconsistency recorded here rather than resolved silently. It runs **unpositioned** unless the maintainer assigns it a slot; [D32](#d32)'s order shifted once already on 2026-09-06 and is not disturbed again for a one-clause skill edit.

Decision.Title: ## D34 — `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` enters at position 4, ahead of `C-ROADMAP-XML`
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-06 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"B it is"*, on three itemized variants — the retirement operation alone, the operation plus the first codification tagging, or a hand edit with no bundle.
**The ruling.** One bundle ships **both** halves: the **ongoing retirement operation** that [F180](#f180) found missing, and the **first `CodifiedIn` / `TaughtIn` tagging** that [F181](#f181) found unreachable. It enters at **position 4**, ahead of [`C-ROADMAP-XML`](#named-bundle-registry).
**The order, in full after this amendment.** **1** `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION` (delivered as `-2`) → **2** `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` (delivered as `-2`, PR #72) → **3** `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` (delivered as `-2`, PR #74) → **4** **`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`** (new) → **5** `C-ROADMAP-XML` → **6** `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` → **7** `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` → **8** `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` → **9** `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` → **10** `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` → **11** `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE`. Seven positions shift by one; **nothing is reordered**.
**Why ahead of `C-ROADMAP-XML`.** The record cannot accept new entries until it can retire old ones. Measured at `67bc55c`: the flush of one session's work breaches both live ceilings, the retirement enforcement cannot fire in any direction — nothing annotates `<PaidBy>`, validation never derives, and the shipped derivation returns **0** live-eligible even when run ([F180](#f180), corrected) — and the decisions genre has no reachable trigger at all. **The ruling stands on the enforcement being inert; it does not rest on the retracted twelve-eligible count.** `C-ROADMAP-XML` converts markdown that **nothing parses** ([F177](#f177)); this unblocks the record itself. The runner-up — shipping only the retirement operation — leaves `rulings.xml` breached with no remedy, because tagging is the only trigger decisions have.
**Name.** `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, naming both halves so the scope is legible from the registry row. **Searched before minting**, 2026-09-06 at `67bc55c`, over `registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml` and every directory under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` for `retire`, `codif`, `taught`, `ratchet` and `ceiling`: the only matches are `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` and `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2`, both archived and both the split rather than the operation. No existing name covers this ground.
**What this amendment falsifies, swept with it.** [D27.1](#d27.1) named `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` at position 6; it is **7** from here. [F178](#f178) named `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` at position 5; it is **6**. [D32](#d32)'s enumerated order is superseded by this one and stands as the dated record of what was true before. Read positions from **this** entry.

Decision.Title: ## D36 — `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` enters at position 6, and every later position shifts by one
Decision.Body:
**Ratified 2026-09-07 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"1 - 6 ok"*, on the authority's recommendation of position 6 after an audit of the live findings.
**The order from here.** **6** `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` → **7** `C-ROADMAP-XML` → **8** `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` → **9** `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` → **10** `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` → **11** `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` → **12** `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` → **13** `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE`. Positions 1–5 are delivered. Read the order from **this** entry.
**Why it goes ahead of `C-ROADMAP-XML`.** `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW` shipped a window that opens by `Δ_retired`, and then could not open it: **zero** live findings are eligible, because **60 of 71** archived bundles have no registry row and their payments are invisible to the derivation ([F187](#f187)). Recording those payments is now the only thing that unblocks the flush, and the same asymmetry that decided [D35](#d35) applies again — the roadmap defect waits without degrading, the buffer does not.
**The scope, as recommended and accepted.** Record payments that already happened rather than fix findings. It is the more caloric option — `F90`, `F90.1` and `F35` alone are 249 lines against a 242-line target, with `F27` and `F38` behind them — and the more deterministic one, since each payment is settled by a symbol or a named test in work already merged, with no governance question and no new behaviour.
**What this amendment falsifies, swept with it.** [D35](#d35) placed `C-ROADMAP-XML` at 6, `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` at 7, `C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY` at 8, `C-CI-CLAIM-PIN` at 9, `C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY` at 10, `C-EFFORT-DEPTH` at 11 and `C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE` at 12. Each is one later from here. [D35](#d35) stands as the dated record of what was true before.
